Hi Aisha — thanks for the points. I reviewed MedSphere's redline and put a counter-redline together with proposed language to address the subprocessors and audit clauses. High-level positions below; I've placed the draft as "Redwood_DPA_v3_neha_redlines.docx" and will push via DocuSign if that works for you.

1) SCCs / transfers: Redwood will execute the latest EU SCCs for transfers of MedSphere personal data from EU residents where required. We reserve the right to substitute equivalent transfer mechanisms if the legal framework changes; we'll notify customers of material changes.

2) Subprocessors: Redwood maintains an up-to-date public registry. For material additions that introduce new categories of processing or new geographic locations we will provide 30 days' notice. If MedSphere reasonably objects within that period because of a demonstrable risk to regulated data, Redwood will work in good faith to provide mitigation (including migration assistance). This is consistent with industry practice — we cannot guarantee an indefinite opt-out without migration support.

3) Audit rights / evidence: we will provide SOC 2 Type II reports under NDA and an executive pen test summary. For deeper evidence we offer a remote evidence review via a secure portal; on-site audits are available on a case-by-case basis subject to confidentiality, scheduling, and cost-recovery. To keep audits focused, our proposed language limits audit scope to systems processing MedSphere data and requires reasonable notice and coordination.

4) Timeframes: we can turn the DPA redline around within 24–48 hours and prepare a DocuSign envelope. If acceptable, we propose execution by 6/9 to keep your pilot schedule intact.

If you have specific clause text you prefer for SCCs or audit scope, send it over and we'll incorporate. Happy to discuss on today's call.

Regards,
